user.title: Add timer
user.description: Put the timer in pairing mode. Choose the Bluetooth address Home Assistant sees.

device_generation.title: Timer generation
device_generation.description: Select the generation of the physical timer you are pairing. Gen 1 (BH1G1) uses a dedicated network key and mesh device ID per timer. Gen 2 (HT25G2) shares the integration network key.

network_key.title: Network key
network_key.description: Shared BLE network key for Gen 2 timers (all Gen 2 devices on this account use the same key). Leave empty to generate a random key, or paste Base64 from the Orbit app (or the same key as 32 hex characters).

gen1_mesh.title: Gen 1 credentials
gen1_mesh.description: Each Gen 1 timer has its own mesh device ID and network key. For {address}, pairing-mode advertisement mesh ID: {discovered}. Put the timer in pairing mode (factory reset if it was already onboarded). Home Assistant listens up to 8 seconds. If the value is "not found" or wrong, enter the BLE Device ID from the Orbit app. Leave the network key empty only for first-time pairing.

error.invalid_key: Invalid key. Use Base64 from the Orbit app or 32 hex characters.
error.cannot_connect: Could not connect or provision the timer. Put it in pairing mode and try again.
error.verify_failed: Handshake worked but the timer did not return device information. Try again.

init.title: Orbit B-hyve
init.description: Add a timer or change Bluetooth status polling.

poll_interval.title: Status polling interval
poll_interval.description: How often Home Assistant reads battery and station status from each timer over Bluetooth. Longer intervals reduce battery use. Turning a station on or off still triggers an immediate update.
